verdicts.opus: C gave the decision-maker the most usable picture. It shows volume falling (CAGR -21.9%, late/early 0.55) with the critical share decomposed, tone set against a defined baseline, and limits placed next to the numbers, including the five unmeasured months. Its weak points are failing follow-ups and an unlinked headline layer. B is cleanly traced but thinner: one series, no critical or CAGR reading. A and D answered honestly from no data or memory and cannot support a decision.
verdicts.gpt: C is the strongest decision brief: it gives a traceable trend, a grounded tone comparison, useful breakdowns, and a reproducible export while distinguishing news coverage from adoption or outcomes. B has fuller trend decomposition, but its unsupported causal account and failed follow-ups weaken its decision value; C’s main gaps are the missing trend CAGR and incomplete placement of data limits.
